newsitem.title: New zealand: NZ shares close easier after bearish surveys.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close easier after bearish surveys.

text.p: * NZ shares close weaker in light trade
* Lion Nathan drops after interim result
* Buyers retreat in face of bearish confidence surveys
Price movements at the close
LAST CHG
317 +6 * NZSC cap index -23.67 at 4,936.10
342 -6 * Volume NZ$27.7 million. Futures -10 at 1115
643 -10 * Other movers - -10 -5
The New Zealand sharemarket eased throughout a quiet day's trading on Monday, with sentiment dominated by two bearish surveys of business confidence.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed down 13.35 points at 2,240.22 on light turnover worth NZ$27.7 million.
Brewer Lion Nathan shed six cents to $3.42 after releasing its interim profit as the market opened.
"After Lion Nathan's interim result the shares weakened but rallied later on moderate volume," said David Evans, a broker with J B Were and Son.
He said Lion's $72.2 million interim profit was in line with market expectations.
"Other than that there are not too many highlights," Evans said.

Patrick Lee, a broker with Lawrence Millton Howarth, said surveys released overnight by the National Bank and the New Zealand Institute of Economic Research showing business confidence at a low ebb had weakened the tone.
"They certainly didn't help," Lee said.
"The economy seems to be stagnating. We are in a vacuum in terms of corporate announcements with uncertainty about earnings."
He said the low turnover suggested prices were falling because buyers were staying on the sidelines rather than because aggressive sellers were driving prices lower.
Brewer DB Group shares rose $1.24 to $2.25 after a capital restructuring that would return $181 million to shareholders.
-- Vernon Small, Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
